parameter.name: JIT_DPHASE_FLOOR_PPM
parameter.what: the phase scatter, in ppm of a period, below which jit.dphase_ar1.seg0 REFUSES instead of reporting. Registered when the value was proposed (#763), not after it landed: the dial replaces a 1e-20 epsilon, and an epsilon is a value nobody swept.

objective.name: worst 44.1k->48k gap in jit.dphase_ar1.seg0
objective.why: the defect the dial exists to fix, stated as the quantity test_extra_features_are_rate_independent measures: the reference corpus is 44.1 kHz and our renders are 48 kHz, so a column that moves between them on the SAME clip is partly a sample-rate detector. It is deliberately NOT the only thing the dial trades. rate_gap improves monotonically as the column is silenced, so on this objective alone an infinite floor wins; sees_real in the same table is the constraint from the other side, and the verdict below is read against both.

range_basis: Five decades bracketing the two quantities this module already has numbers for, chosen before the sweep ran: the 44.1k->48k phase artefact at ~0.8 ppm (test_the_rate_tolerance_is_far_below_the_effect, and RATE_TOL_ABS['ppm'] = 20 is the floor already stated against it for the sibling column jit.phasejit_ppm), and 0.1 % per-period jitter at ~5.7e3 ppm of phase scatter.
0 is the behaviour that shipped before #763: the guard was `d.std() > _EPS` with _EPS = 1e-20, which nothing real is ever below, so 0 and the shipped epsilon are the same point on this dial.

200 and 2000 are above the smallest real mechanism the column must see (+0.5 Hz of static detuning, 54.53 ppm) and are on the grid ON PURPOSE, so the dial's upper bound is a measured row rather than an assertion. They are the rows where sees_real drops from 7 to 6.

decision_rule.why: the decision this dial serves is whether a floor changes what the rate-independence control can see, so the threshold comes from that control's granularity. The control cannot resolve a gap below RATE_TOL_ABS['ratio'] = 0.02 ar1 for a correlation column, and this objective never exceeds 0.43 anywhere on the grid, so 2 % relative is at most 0.0086 ar1 -- strictly TIGHTER than the control's own resolution everywhere. Tighter is the conservative direction: a rule finer than the control can split points the control would call equal, which can only add groups, never manufacture a plateau.

evidence.instrument: jitter_features itself, through its dphase_floor_ppm override and trace hook -- the shipped gate, not a reimplementation of it. Stimuli are the module's own _square and its band-limited _resample, so the rate pair is the one the rate-independence test compares, and the mechanism panel is exactly the stimulus set test_static_detuning_is_not_reported_as_drift depends on. Each jittered entry asserts its jitter survived the generator's whole-sample period rounding and REFUSES if it did not. Measured on python 3.12.3 / numpy 2.5.4 / scipy 1.18.1.

prediction.basis: Stated from three quantities, none of which is a point on this sweep, so the measurement can contradict it. (a) A square generated at 44.1 kHz has whole-sample periods, so its phase residual there is float rounding of a unit-scale phase and reads 0 ppm to the printed precision. (b) The same clip band-limited to 48 kHz carries resample_poly residue, which this module already measures at ~0.8 ppm. (c) The jittered rate-panel entries scatter ~5.7e3 ppm. A floor makes exactly one refusal decision per clip, so two floors falling in the same interval of {0, 0.8, 5.7e3} must give bit-identical numbers and two in different intervals cannot. 0 refuses nothing. 0.2 straddles (a) and (b): it refuses the 44.1 kHz side of every jitterless entry and not the 48 kHz side, so it must differ from 0 and from everything above (b). 2, 20, 200 and 2000 all sit between (b) and (c): same decision on every rate-panel entry, one run. Note this prediction is about the OBJECTIVE only -- 200 and 2000 differ from 20 on the constraint, which is a different column and is why the shipped value is not 200.

verdict.summary: On the objective the dial is a cliff and then a plateau: 0.43 ar1 of rate gap at floor 0 (including a sign flip at 440 Hz and another at 660 Hz), 0.35 at 0.2, and 0.0011 everywhere from 2 ppm up -- that residue being the jittered entries' own 44.1k->48k reproducibility, not the defect. The CONSTRAINT is what picks a point on that plateau: sees_real falls from 7 to 6 at 200 ppm, where +0.5 Hz of static detuning (54.53 ppm of scatter) stops being reported and test_static_detuning_is_not_reported_as_drift goes silent instead of red. So the dial's usable range is 2..20 ppm, a single decade, and 20 is its top -- taken from RATE_TOL_ABS['ppm'], the floor this module already states for the sibling column, rather than fitted to these numbers.

limits: rate_gap alone is not a sufficient criterion for this dial and the record says so twice on purpose. tools/sensitivity.py reads only the objective column, so it reports a four-point plateau from 2 to 2000; the sees_real column in the same artefact is what that cannot see, and it cuts the plateau at 20.

The usable range is one decade (2..20 ppm), bounded below by resampler residue at ~0.8 ppm and above by the +0.5 Hz beat at 54.53 ppm -- a factor of 70, not of 1000. The shipped 20 sits 25x above the noise and 2.7x below the smallest mechanism, and that 2.7x is the tight edge. test_the_dphase_floor_refuses_the_input_that_defeats_it asserts both margins so neither can close unnoticed.

An earlier version of this record swept a floor on the per-cycle period error (np.diff(lin).std()), the quantity ar1 is computed from. That is the wrong quantity: the +0.5 Hz beat has only 4.56 ppm of it against 0.80 ppm of noise, a factor of 5.7, and a 20 ppm floor there silenced the beating control. The ds columns of the detail tables are kept so that refutation stays visible rather than being a sentence about a file nobody has.

Inside the plateau the objective is not exactly zero: 0.0011 ar1 is the 44.1k->48k reproducibility of the JITTERED rate-panel entries, which do have something to measure. The jitterless entries contribute exactly 0 there because both rates are refused.

The panel is synthetic squares and tones, not corpus audio. It establishes where the floor sits relative to float rounding, resampler residue, generated jitter, static detuning and a glide. How many rows of a real discrimination run fall under the floor is a separate, unmeasured question -- the reference corpus is not on this host; counted in issue #768.
